instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the sausage and beef with 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook, breaking the meat up with a spoon, until it's browned, about 6 minutes.
Add the diced onion and cook, stirring, until it's soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
Stir in the marinara, broth, oregano, basil, dried parsley, pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, put the lasagna noodles in a large bowl of hot tap water and stir them now and then for 4 minutes. Drain them and break them into bite-size pieces.
In a bowl, stir together the ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan and 1 tbsp of chopped fresh parsley.
Take the lid off the soup, add the noodles and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're tender.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top each with a spoonful of the cheese mixture and a little of the remaining 1 tbsp chopped parsley.
Leftover soup keeps in the fridge for 3 days. The noodles keep soaking up broth, so add a splash of water when you reheat it.
method_notes: Lead is Amanda's Cookin' (4.95 from 20): browned beef and sausage, jarred marinara with broth, noodles soaked first, and a ricotta mixture spooned on top. Well Plated (5 from 7 ratings) adds butternut squash, kale and cream, and the soup is finished with ricotta balls; those were left out. Halved from the lead's 8 servings, with the onion softened first instead of going in raw.
